proposals.before: Liang then advised Xiang Liang: 'You have already established the Chu successor, but among the Han princes Lord Hengyang Cheng Xian can be established as king, to further build alliances.'
proposals.after: Liang then advised Xiang Liang: 'You have already established the Chu successor, but among the Han princes Lord Hengyang, Cheng, is worthy and can be established as king, to further build alliances.'
proposals.reason: 賢 is the predicate worthy describing 橫陽君成, not a personal name Cheng Xian.

proposals.before: He appointed Liang as Han envoy, with the King of Han leading over a thousand men raiding Han territory to the west, capturing several cities, but Qin always recaptured them, going back and forth as roaming troops in Yingchuan.
proposals.after: He appointed Liang as Han Minister over the Masses, and with the King of Han they led over a thousand men raiding Han territory to the west, capturing several cities, but Qin always recaptured them, going back and forth as roaming troops in Yingchuan.
proposals.reason: 申徒 is the Han office equivalent to 司徒, not envoy.

proposals.before: Liang once idly strolled leisurely on the bridge at Xiapi, when an old man in coarse clothing came to where Liang was, directly dropped his shoe down into the bridge, turned and told Liang: 'Young man, go down and get my shoe!'
proposals.after: Liang once idly strolled leisurely on the bridge at Xiapi, when an old man in coarse clothing came to where Liang was, deliberately dropped his shoe off the bridge, turned and told Liang: 'Young man, go down and get my shoe!'
proposals.reason: 直墮其履圯下 means the shoe was dropped from the bridge, not into the structure.

proposals.before: When Duke Pei came from Luoyang south out of Xuan Yuan, Liang led troops following Duke Pei, capturing over ten Han cities, defeating Yang Xiong's army.
proposals.after: When Duke Pei came from Luoyang south out of Xuanyuan, Liang led troops following Duke Pei, capturing over ten Han cities, defeating Yang Xiong's army.
proposals.reason: 轘轅 is the place-name Xuanyuan; the spaced 'Xuan Yuan' obscures the pass name.

proposals.before: Pursued north to Lantian, fought again, Qin troops utterly defeated.
proposals.after: He pursued the routed enemy to Lantian, fought again, and the Qin troops were utterly defeated.
proposals.reason: 逐北 means pursuing a defeated force, not traveling north; the silent subject continues the Duke of Pei from the previous sentence.

proposals.before: Thus, reached Xianyang, Qin prince Zi Ying surrendered to Duke Pei.
proposals.after: Thus they reached Xianyang, and Ziying, King of Qin, surrendered to Duke Pei.
proposals.reason: 秦王 is king, not prince, and 子嬰 is the personal name Ziying.

proposals.before: They pressed on to Xianyang, where Ziying, the last King of Qin, surrendered to the Duke of Pei.
proposals.after: They pressed on to Xianyang, where Ziying, King of Qin, surrendered to the Duke of Pei.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names him 秦王子嬰 and does not call him the last king; 'last' is an inserted gloss.

proposals.before: When Liang reached Han, the King of Xiang—because Liang had followed the King of Han—refused to let King Cheng of Han return to his domain and instead forced him to travel east in his retinue.
proposals.after: When Liang reached Han, King Cheng of Han—because Liang had followed the King of Han—was not allowed by the King of Xiang to return to his domain, and was instead taken east in the King of Xiang's retinue.
proposals.reason: The Chinese topic is 韓王成 and the 以-clause explains why 項王 would not send 成 to his state; the current English makes the King of Xiang the opening subject and blurs Cheng as the detained party.

proposals.before: When they reached Xiayi, the King of Han dismounted and sat upon his saddle, asking, 'I would give up everything east of the passes. Who among the lords is worthy enough to share the task of defeating Chu?'
proposals.after: When they reached Xiayi, the King of Han dismounted and sat upon his saddle, asking, 'I would give up everything east of the passes. Who can share the achievement with me?'
proposals.reason: 誰可與共功者 does not name 'the lords' or 'the task of defeating Chu'; those additions invent referents and a goal not present in this sentence.

proposals.before: Zhang Liang replied: 'Your servant requests to borrow the eating sticks in front to plan for the great king.'
proposals.after: Zhang Liang replied: 'Your servant requests to borrow the chopsticks in front to plan for the great king.'
proposals.reason: Literal 'eating sticks' is an unnatural calque for 箸, which are chopsticks.

proposals.before: The emperor wished to depose the crown prince, establish Lady Qi's son King Zhao of You.
proposals.after: The emperor wished to depose the crown prince and establish Lady Qi's son Ruyi, King of Zhao.
proposals.reason: Literal English turns 趙王如意 into 'King Zhao of You', reversing the title (King of Zhao) and given name (Ruyi).

proposals.before: The ministers around him were all Shandong people, many advised the emperor to establish capital in Luoyang: 'Luoyang east has Chenggao, west has Xiaomeng, with the Yellow River behind, facing Yi and Luo—its fortifications are also sufficient to rely on.'
proposals.after: The ministers around him were all Shandong people, many advised the emperor to establish the capital in Luoyang: 'Luoyang east has Chenggao, west has Xiao and Mian, with the Yellow River behind, facing Yi and Luo—its fortifications are also sufficient to rely on.'
proposals.reason: 殽黽 are the Xiao and Mian (passes); the literal fuses them into the nonexistent place 'Xiaomeng'.

proposals.before: Guanzhong has Xiao to the left, Han to the right, fertile plains a thousand li, south has Bashu's wealth, north has the Xiongnu's advantages, blocking three sides to defend, alone using one side east to control the feudal lords.
proposals.after: Guanzhong has Xiao and Hangu to the left, Long and Shu to the right, fertile plains a thousand li, south has Ba-Shu's wealth, north has the advantage of the Hu pasturelands, blocking three sides to defend, alone using one side east to control the feudal lords.
proposals.reason: 左殽函 is Xiao and Hangu, not 'Han'; 胡苑 is Hu pastureland, not specifically 'the Xiongnu'.

proposals.before: Thus, the emperor set up wine, enfeoffed Yong Chi as Marquis of Shifang, and urgently urged the chancellor and superintendent to determine merits and carry out enfeoffments.
proposals.after: Thus, the emperor set up wine, enfeoffed Yong Chi as Marquis of Shifang, and urgently urged the chancellor and the imperial secretary (yushi) to determine merits and carry out enfeoffments.
proposals.reason: 御史 is the imperial secretary/censor, not a generic 'superintendent'.

proposals.before: Your servant has heard 'a mother who loves her child embraces him', now Lady Qi serves day and night, King Zhao You Yi is constantly held in front, the emperor says 'I will never let an unworthy son be placed above a beloved son', clearly his replacing the crown prince's position is certain.
proposals.after: Your servant has heard 'a mother who loves her child embraces him'; now Lady Qi serves day and night, Ruyi, King of Zhao, is constantly held in front; the emperor says 'I will never let an unworthy son be placed above a beloved son'; clearly his replacing the crown prince's position is certain.
proposals.reason: Literal English misreads 趙王如意 as 'King Zhao You Yi' rather than Ruyi, King of Zhao.

proposals.before: Gaozu departed from difficulties several times, yet the Marquis of Liu constantly had meritorious strength—how can this not be called heaven?
proposals.after: Gaozu encountered difficulties several times, yet the Marquis of Liu constantly had meritorious strength—how can this not be called Heaven?
proposals.reason: 離困 means to meet with hardship (罹), not to depart from difficulties.

proposals.before: I considered this person in planning to be stalwart and extraordinary, until seeing his portrait, his appearance was like a woman or beautiful girl.
proposals.after: I had supposed this man to be stalwart and extraordinary, until seeing his portrait; his appearance was like that of a woman or a beautiful girl.
proposals.reason: 計 here is the historian's supposition about physique, not 'in planning'.

proposals.before: The old man whom Zifang had met on the bridge at Xiapi, the one who gave him the book of Taigong — thirteen years later, while accompanying Emperor Gao through Jibei, Zhang Liang came upon a yellow stone at the foot of Mount Gucheng, just as the old man had foretold. He took it and enshrined it with reverence.
proposals.after: The old man whom Zifang had met on the bridge at Xiapi, the one who gave him the book of Taigong — thirteen years later, while accompanying Emperor Gao through Jibei, he came upon a yellow stone at the foot of Mount Gucheng, just as the old man had foretold. He took it and enshrined it with reverence.
proposals.reason: Chinese continues with silent subject 子房; inserting the surname Zhang Liang is not in the source sentence.
